filesChanged: packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/text.ts — clipMiddle and escapedHead, a middle clip that splits no character and no entity.

packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/rules-check.ts — describeAsks clips in the middle, bounds an ask's id at 128 bytes and floors each ask's text; readAsks and runRulesCheck tell "no new ask" from "the read failed, so none was judged", which answers the new outcome unjudged.

packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/askgate-core.ts — the breaker counts refusals per thing (each new ask a call opens, or the call as a whole), with covers(), Revise and count() gone; the warning and the pass are about the same thing.
packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/decision-record.ts and packages/pi-envoy/scripts/askgate-report.ts — the unjudged outcome through the record and both report modes, with its own count.
packages/pi-envoy/README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the askgate-core header — the stale 8 KiB and left-out-ask sentences replaced by what the code does, the new outcome and the new counts.
The tests beside each: askgate.test.ts, decision-record.test.ts, askgate-report.test.ts.
trickyParts: A middle clip of escaped text must not cut inside a UTF-8 character or an `&…;` entity at either edge, or the clip itself could re-open a tag; the head moves back and the tail forward until both are clean.
The id can be cut where the text cannot: no rule reads the id, and the refusal names an ask by its number and its opening.

The breaker's counter is per thing while its reset stays per target, because an allow, a rebuttal or a trip sends a call on that target and so ends every loop there; clearing more than the call's own things can only cost a review, never give a pass.

One departure from the architect's literal key, stated rather than hidden: a charter refusal of a call that opens asks counts on those asks rather than on the whole-call key. With the literal key either a charter loop on one ask never ends, or two refused plain edits give a brand-new ask a free pass; the test covers both halves.
deviations: The round-2 fixture dispatch://INFRA-362 was closed after the tester released it, so this round's live runs use a new unassigned fixture, dispatch://INFRA-365.
No simplify pass: one per pull request, run in the first implementing round.

The two surfaces the reviewer left on the risk line stay there — the device path, which no Legion pod mounts, and a de-duplication read Dispatch never actually failed — both covered by unit cases, as the architect accepted.
openQuestions: sjawhar/legion#2159 is still open and this branch carries its commits; the architect watches it and the plan's "when #2159 merges" step runs before the review round that approves the head.
discoveredComplexity: All four findings of this round are the same fault as round 1's: a bound, a counter or a failed read quietly deciding that an ask is not judged, with the entry still reading as judged and clean. The counts added over the two rounds — asks cut, asks judged in part, asks judged not at all — are what make each of those visible to the session that reads Dispatch.

The live two-ask run shows why a unit test was not enough here: the charter check's own reason named the clip ("Each copy is cut off at 'parquet f'"), which is what proves the rules match came from a clipped body rather than from a body that happened to fit.
